stages.title: Preflight
stages.subtitle: Prepare to succeed.
stages.description: Skim once so you know what exists. Then come back when the acronym shows up in a real meeting. These references answer the first questions every founder hits: who buys, how they buy, and where the money flows.

resources.title: Contracting Cone
resources.description: The one-page chart that answers 'which contract vehicle?' in about a minute. Open it whenever someone names a vehicle you don't recognize.

resources.title: FAR for Startups
resources.description: The rulebook every contracting officer lives by. You will never read it cover to cover. Search it when a clause number lands in your inbox.

resources.title: Contract Types Explained
resources.description: FFP, T&M, CPFF, CPIF. Check this before you agree to a contract type, because each one moves risk in a different direction.

resources.title: Understanding PPBE
resources.description: Why the money you need this year was decided two years ago. Ten minutes here explains most of the delays you will ever encounter.

resources.title: Signals Feed
resources.description: Live intel from Breaking Defense, ExecutiveGov, and Merge Combinator analysis. Scan it weekly; demand signals show up here before they show up in solicitations.

resources.title: Defense Ecosystem Map
resources.description: Who sits where across commands, agencies, and innovation units. Pull it up before any meeting with an office you have not worked with.

stages.title: Spot
stages.subtitle: Where you are and what's next.
stages.description: Match your technology to demand that already exists: SBIR topics, CSOs, OTAs, or a problem sponsor with a real budget. These are the boards to check and the pathways to compare when you decide where to aim.

resources.title: Finding Problem Sponsors
resources.description: How to find the person who owns your problem and has the standing to champion it. Read before you cold-email anyone with a .mil address.

resources.title: AFWERX Engagement Pathways
resources.description: Spark, Prime, and Ventures compared. Check which door fits before you knock on the Air Force.

resources.title: DIU Commercial Solutions Opening
resources.description: How DIU buys commercial technology. Read this if your product already sells in the private sector.

resources.title: Other Transaction Authority Guide
resources.description: What an OTA can do that a FAR contract cannot. Worth knowing before someone offers you one.

resources.title: Opportunities Board
resources.description: Live solicitations from SBIR, DARPA, DIU, and SAM.gov in one feed. Check it the way you check the weather.

resources.title: SBIR Topic Search
resources.description: Every open SBIR/STTR topic across the government. Search your keywords quarterly; topics recycle.

resources.title: Pricing Strategies for Government Contracts
resources.description: How to price FFP, T&M, and CPFF work without leaving money or margin behind. Open before you write a number in a proposal.

stages.title: Ready for Launch
stages.subtitle: Get connected.
stages.description: The paperwork stage. Proposals, CMMC, ITAR, CUI, clearances. None of it is fun and all of it gates contracts. Return to each reference when that gate is in front of you.

resources.title: Phase I Proposal Guide
resources.description: The official tutorial from the people who score your proposal. Read it the week before you write, not the night before you submit.

resources.title: CMMC 2.0 Requirements
resources.description: Which maturity level your contracts will demand and what it takes to get there. Check early; remediation takes months.

resources.title: ITAR Basics for Startups
resources.description: Whether your technology is export-controlled and what registration requires. Answer this before you demo to anyone foreign-owned.

resources.title: CUI Marking Handbook
resources.description: How to mark and handle controlled unclassified information. Keep it open the first time a CUI document lands on your desk.

resources.title: Security Clearance Process
resources.description: What clearances take, cost, and require of your people. Start here before you promise cleared staff in a proposal.

resources.title: Proposal Writing Playbook
resources.description: The Merge Combinator framework for structuring SBIR and OTA proposals that score. Use it as the outline for your next submission.

stages.title: Tension
stages.subtitle: Build to full power.
stages.description: The prototype worked and now the budget cycle is the enemy. These are the bridge programs, transition guides, and evidence frameworks to open when production feels far away. This stage is why founders bookmark this page.

resources.title: Valley of Death Survival Guide
resources.description: John Ferry's 351-page playbook for the crossing. Not a sit-down read. Search it by chapter when you hit the specific wall it names.

resources.title: DON Phase III Guidebook
resources.description: The Navy's own manual for converting funded work into production contracts. Cite it back to them when a contracting office hesitates.

resources.title: APFIT: Procurement & Fielding Funds
resources.description: Eight-figure OUSD(R&E) money built to jump prototypes into procurement. Check the eligibility window every cycle; it moves.

resources.title: STRATFI / TACFI Bridge Funding
resources.description: AFWERX bridge funding that matches government dollars with private capital between Phase II and Phase III. Read before your Phase II ends, not after.

resources.title: The Interceptor Math Is Broken
resources.description: Merge Combinator analysis on why affordable mass wins. Steal the framing for your own production story.

resources.title: Valley of Death Navigator
resources.description: An interactive decision framework for prototype-to-production transitions. Work through it when you are choosing between paths.

resources.title: Operator Validation Toolkit
resources.description: Templates for turning operator enthusiasm into documented evidence a PM can cite. Use after every exercise and demo.

stages.title: Launch
stages.subtitle: Go operational.
stages.description: Production, follow-ons, teaming, and the team itself. The questions get bigger and rarer at this stage. Keep these references close; each one exists for a conversation you will eventually have.

resources.title: Color of Money
resources.description: Which appropriation can legally buy what you sell. Check it before every pilot conversation; the wrong color kills deals late.

resources.title: From Combine to Series A: Ulysses
resources.description: What operator-validated formation produced, from Combine to Series A. Show it to skeptical investors.

resources.title: The Army Is Rewriting How It Buys Technology
resources.description: Merge Combinator analysis of acquisition restructured around software velocity. Context for every Army conversation you will have this year.

resources.title: Prime & Subcontracting Rules
resources.description: The SBA rules on teaming, flow-down clauses, and subcontracting plans. Read before you sign anything a prime sends.

resources.title: The $16B Alignment Problem
resources.description: Merge Combinator analysis on whether the system can absorb the capital flowing in. Useful when your investors ask about the market.

resources.title: Production Contract Playbook
resources.description: Follow-on strategies, sole-source justification, and teaming structures. Open when the production conversation starts.

resources.title: Prime Teaming & Subcontractor Strategy
resources.description: How to structure prime partnerships that scale instead of smother. Read before the term sheet, not after.
